From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@atlasops.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: billing@atlasops.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden token plateau + latency variance — need a checkpoint

Hi Soojin,

We’re seeing an unexpected flattening in token consumption across our chat assistants since last Thursday and a few intermittent latency spikes on peak queries (p99 up ~340ms from baseline ~210ms). Our product team is worried this is limiting user sessions and pushing more retried calls. From AtlasOps’ billing view the projected monthly token burn is roughly 18M tokens but the last 10 days point to a 12% deviation versus the previous quarter cadence.

Can Redwood help us diagnose whether this is workload-driven (prompt changes / batching) or if we’re hitting a capacity/throughput limits on the Dedicated pool? Also want to understand cost/benefit of a short burst vs increasing committed capacity for Q3.

I attached the snippet of our token ledger and a sample session trace. Happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks,
Maria Lopez
Head of ML, AtlasOps

Attachments: q2-token-performance.csv (csv, 42KB); sample_session_trace.txt (txt, 8KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@atlasops.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden token plateau + latency variance — need a checkpoint

Hi Maria — thanks for the data and for flagging this. Looping in Ben (customer success — capacity/ops) and Marissa (rev ops) to pull performance telemetry and billing alignment. Initial read: the ledger you sent shows a shift in average prompt length (tokens per request) and a small increase in request rate variance at 2–3 hour windows. Both can show up as a "plateau" in total tokens while request patterns change. That alone wouldn’t explain the latency tail — that looks like transient queueing on our Dedicated pool at specific hot-shard intervals.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben to share server-side latency breakdown and recent autoscaler events (last 7d).
- We'll run a 48-hour targeted cache warm / prefix-KV test for a subset of your routes (no code changes on your side).
- If hotspots persist we can propose a temporary 4-week burst (adds +25% GPU headroom) while we validate commit uplift economics.

We can do a 30-min sync today at 2pm PT. Does that work?

Best,
Sojin
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192

Thanks Soojin. Quick telemetry snapshot attached (attachment: kv-cache-heatmap.png). Highlights:
- P99 latency correlates with short-lived spike in concurrent requests to model-v2 across 13:40–14:05 PT on 7/12 and 7/13.
- Autoscaler executed a single scale event but the scale ramp (cold-start container GPU init) added ~80–120ms per affected request during the transition window.
- We observed reduced effective cache hit rate (~6% lower) on the top-3 routes — likely due to prompt variation you mentioned.

Recommended immediate actions:
1) Run the 48h targeted KV warm-up on the 3 routes (we'll coordinate with your SRE to pin traffic). Expected impact: ~7–12% token reduction and p99 improvement.
2) Activate a 4-week burst (25% headroom) while we run a deeper root-cause runbook. Cost estimate: incremental $6k/week on top of current committed monthly spend.
3) If AtlasOps prefers a longer-term uplift, propose a staged +40% committed tier with a 6-month lookback credit for unused burst. I’ve sketched numbers in an attached PDF (proposed-commit-term.pdf).

Maria — happy to run the 2pm PT sync and present the telemetry.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
